answer: Each identity claims one forge mirror: a forge-cast plate with an 85-credit bond on its serial. It files thickness and polish grade each epoch; an auditor checks reflectance against the mirror polish table, with an echo check within 2%. Over 3% off, a reused serial, or a shared plate burns the bond and voids both. The first claim costs 29, the kth 29+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7022 and 1000 fakes cost 3,525,500 plus 85,000 locked. A rented-mirror ring fails: one plate yields one signed reading per epoch, so lenders go without and copies carry the wrong key. An honest agent pays 29 once.
